statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 3 and far below the block threshold because CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z, leaving no Nasdaq-100 price path to score; the last observed path, Friday's record 31,017.53 intraday high fully retraced into a 30,807.93 close in the lower quarter of the 30,737.07-31,017.53 range with VIX down 6.59% to 15.31, was orderly two-way discovery rather than the extension pattern Tail measures. Stress rises a point to 75 in the high band because the Riyadh refinery fire now has independent physical corroboration from a Reuters witness, an AFP journalist and NASA FIRMS thermal detections, while Saudi authorities and Aramco have still not confirmed an attack, damage, casualties or any refining, production or export impact. Confidence eases to 84 on independently re-verified session levels, yields, oil and calendar against an unresolved damage question and no live price path.
recommendation: Tail stays in the low band for the first 20 scored hours, so the deterministic mapping remains EA_ON and green through 21:00Z. The three hours from the 22:00Z restart carry Tail 21, 23 and 21, which maps to WATCH and yellow: that is the mildest cautionary band and reflects a dated discontinuity meeting thin Sunday-evening liquidity while a claimed strike on Saudi refining capacity is still unquantified. Tail returns to the low band at 19 by 01:00Z on 5 October. The Saudi cash session from roughly 07:00Z to 12:00Z is the only live venue with direct exposure to the strike; under the inherited delayed-evidence rule it can inform Stress and Confidence but cannot establish current Nasdaq-100 structure or the current action. A narrow danger window is published across the three restart hours as a dated discontinuity checkpoint. The next scheduled U.S. macro checkpoint is ISM Services at 14:00Z on 5 October, with FOMC minutes on 7 October.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 3 with no Nasdaq-100 price path to score, while independent corroboration of a refinery fire near Riyadh against still-absent Saudi confirmation lifts Stress to 75 and keeps the three hours after the 22:00Z restart in the watch band
body:
Friday 2 October remains the last traded session and its levels were independently re-verified for this publication. The Nasdaq-100 closed at a record 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00% from a 30,501.56 previous close, inside a 30,737.07-31,017.53 session range whose high is also the 52-week high. The detail that matters most for this framework is unchanged: the new intraday record at 31,017.53 was fully retraced and the index finished in the lower quarter of its own daily range. That is orderly two-way price discovery, not the shallow-pullback extension or failed-retracement pattern that defines Tail, so Tail holds at 3. VIX closed at 15.31, down 6.59% from 16.39 inside a 15.30-16.24 range, confirming volatility decay into the halt.

The session's driver was the September employment report: nonfarm payrolls rose 29,000 against a 90,000 consensus, the unemployment rate was 4.2% against 4.1% expected, monthly wage growth slowed to 0.1% and annual wage growth to 3.0%. Equities read that as cementing a Fed hold at the 28 October meeting, but the curve did not follow. The 2-year finished at 4.8414%, up 5.44 basis points, and the 10-year at 5.2939%, up 5.99 basis points, so a soft labour print was met with a higher long end. The Federal Reserve H.15 release has been re-checked and still publishes only through 1 October, where the 2-year stands at 4.78% and the 10-year at 5.24%, so Friday's reversal is carried from market reporting rather than from the official series.

The material change since the previous hour is corroboration rather than attribution. The claimed Houthi ballistic missile and drone strike on an Aramco facility in Riyadh now carries independent physical evidence: a Reuters witness reported a large plume of smoke and fire in the vicinity of the facility, an AFP journalist separately described flames and smoke at Aramco's Riyadh refinery south of the capital with firefighters working the site, and NASA FIRMS satellite monitoring registered higher-intensity VIIRS thermal hits across the refinery. What has not changed is the part that governs risk transmission. Saudi authorities have not confirmed that the facility was attacked, Aramco did not respond to a request for comment, and there is no confirmed information on damage extent, casualties, or any disruption to refining, production or fuel supply. Saudi counter-strikes on Yemen were reported hours after the fire, so the retaliation cycle is active in both directions.

Two threads surfaced during research were checked and excluded as current evidence because they belong to earlier incidents: the Aramco Jazan refinery attack dates to 9 August 2026, and the claimed strike on Aramco facilities at Yanbu and a target in Riyadh dates to 24 September 2026. Neither is part of this weekend's event and neither is used here.

Energy is the transmission channel to watch and it is two-sided. Trading Economics puts the 2 October settlements at $91.11 for WTI, down 1.90%, and $102.25 for Brent, down 0.06%, with WTI up 49.66% and Brent up 58.45% year on year, so the complex is already carrying a large geopolitical premium before this weekend's event. Against that, the G7 has announced plans to release 100 million barrels of reserves over the next four months, a stated supply-side offset that caps the conditional Monday gap. Oil futures are also closed, so no venue has priced the fire.

Stress therefore rises one point to 75 and stays inside the high band: the physical corroboration is firmer than an hour ago, but the quantum that would matter for Nasdaq-100 earnings and rates, an actual throughput or export loss, is unverified and partially offset. Tail is unchanged at 3 because Tail scores a price path and there is no price path: the CME equity-index complex has been halted since Friday 21:00Z and reopens at 22:00Z on Sunday. Confidence eases one point to 84, high but not higher, reflecting independently re-verified index, volatility, yield, oil and calendar evidence set against an unresolved official damage question and the absence of live price discovery.

The shared Finviz context file was read as required and is not usable this hour: its collectionStatus is partial and its generatedAt of 29 September is roughly four days old, far outside the 90-minute freshness contract, with its calendar and futures sections both unavailable. Under the inherited fail-open rule that is recorded and ignored rather than allowed to delay or degrade publication, and the full independent research above stands on its own.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments and no slot required an unavailable entry. The window opens at 02:00Z on 3 October with Tail 9 and Stress 65 under a normal mode and decays as the halt takes hold: Tail falls from 9 to 3 by 12:00Z and stays at 3 for the remaining thirteen hours. Stress troughs at 52 around 14:00Z and then climbs steadily to 74 by 01:00Z on 4 October as the energy and Gulf escalation threads reopened and produced the fire at the Riyadh refinery. Confidence held in a narrow 82 to 88 range throughout, consistent with verified session levels and no live price path. No historical opinion was revised.
outlookSummary: Twenty of the 24 forecast hours fall inside the CME equity-index weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them. Tail is held at 3 through 06:00Z, ticks up across the Saudi cash session, then rises along the restart approach to 18 by 21:00Z, mapping to EA_ON and green for those 20 hours. The three hours from 22:00Z carry Tail 21, 23 and 21, crossing into the watch band and mapping to WATCH and yellow on a dated discontinuity, thin opening liquidity and an unquantified claimed strike on Saudi refining capacity; Tail then returns to the low band at 19 by 01:00Z. Stress runs from 75 to a peak of 79 and stays inside the high band before easing to 76 once a venue has priced the weekend's news for three hours. Confidence eases from 84 to a low of 77 before the restart as Friday's levels age, lifts during the Saudi session and recovers to 85 once live prices return. The dominant mode shifts from normal to mixed four hours before the restart on genuinely two-sided reopening paths.
